title: Universal Basic Income (UBI)
rootClaim: Governments should guarantee an unconditional basic income to every adult citizen regardless of income or employment status.

branches.text: Poverty Elimination, Human Dignity, and Automation Shield: UBI creates a reliable economic floor and simplifies welfare bureaucracy.

children.text: Elimination of Welfare Traps: Unlike means-tested welfare, UBI does not penalize recipients with benefit cliffs when they secure employment.
Fiscal Expense & Taxes: Funding a universal payout requires massive tax hikes that threaten economic productivity and capital investment.
Bureaucratic Consolidation: Eliminating redundant welfare agencies and capturing automated productivity via land-value or VAT taxes fully funds UBI.
Bargaining Power & Autonomy: Guaranteed basic income allows workers to refuse abusive workplace conditions and pursue education or caregiving.
Labor Supply Reduction: Universal payouts remove the imperative to work, leading to systemic labor shortages in essential low-wage jobs.
Empirical Pilot Results: Real-world UBI trials demonstrate minimal reduction in working hours, mostly concentrated in education and child-rearing.

branches.text: Economic Inefficiency, Inflation, and Recipient Moral Hazard: UBI is inefficient compared to targeted social safety nets.

children.text: Deadweight Loss of Universality: Distributing public funds to high-income earners who do not need assistance is an inefficient allocation of limited state revenue.
Stigma Eradication: Universal programs command broader middle-class political support and eliminate the social degradation of means-testing.
Cost-Push Inflation: Universal liquidity increases consumer demand for basic goods without increasing production capacity, triggering price inflation that erodes UBI purchasing power.
Production Elasticity: Increased purchasing power among low-income households stimulates business competition and supply-side capacity expansion.

definitions.description: A periodic cash payment unconditionally delivered to all citizens on an individual basis, without means-testing or work requirement.
A situation where welfare benefits are withdrawn so quickly as earned income rises that workers are left no better off.
The practice of restricting eligibility for government assistance to individuals whose income falls below a specific threshold.
A levy on the unimproved value of land, often proposed as an efficient, non-distortive source of revenue for UBI.
